hints.title: Composite Multiple Sieve Elimination
hints.text: Trial division for every individual number takes too long. How can marking composite multiples eliminate non-prime candidates in bulk?

hints.title: Square Factor Starting Invariant
hints.text: Starting from each prime p, composite multiples below p squared have already been marked by smaller prime factors, so sieving starts at p * p.

hints.title: Eratosthenes Sieve Mark and Count Procedure
hints.text: Allocate a boolean table up to n initialized to true. Set indices 0 and 1 to false. For each prime p from 2 up to sqrt(n), mark all multiples of p beginning at p squared as false. Count remaining true entries.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: input element count or target integer bound
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N log log N) time and O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Testing divisibility individually for each number up to n takes O(N * sqrt(N)) time, exceeding limits for n = 5,000,000.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: The Sieve of Eratosthenes achieves O(N log log N) time using an O(N) boolean array.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should implement the classical sieve starting multiple marking at p * p and optimizing loop bound to sqrt(n).
